minutes.headline: New planning and economic development director hired for Lunenburg, starts February 2
minutes.summary: The committee learned the town has hired a planning and economic development director (Stephen Wallace, starting Feb. 2) and that PJ Keating has agreed to host the 2026 town official meet-and-greet at no cost to the committee. Most of the meeting was spent on a proposed bylaw to let non-restaurant businesses (prompted by a nail salon wanting to allow BYOB at bachelorette-party events) hold BYOB alcohol events, with no vote taken and the group deciding instead to meet with visiting town counsel the next day. The committee also set its February 10 agenda (an introduction from the new director, a town-counsel update, a business overview, and a presentation from Leominster's economic development office) and approved its December 9 minutes.

budget_items.topic: 2026 Town Official Meet and Greet hosting
budget_items.what_was_said: PJ Keating agreed to host the annual meet-and-greet and supply an outdoor heater, tables, chairs and catered food at no charge, which members said would take a significant cost/logistics burden off the committee. The door was said to remain open for additional local business sponsorship of the event.

decisions.decision: Next regular meeting set for February 10 at 5:30 despite one member's scheduling conflict, since a quorum of three is achievable.
Several members will sign up for the 1:00 p.m. slot with visiting town counsel on January 14 to ask about the BYOB/change-of-use bylaw questions rather than take committee action that day.
Bylaw amendment discussion will be picked up again after members meet with town counsel, with any additional member questions to be raised at that meeting.

Committee members must email Josie their topics/questions for both the Steven Wallace introduction and the Leominster presentation by the following Tuesday, since Josie will be traveling and unreachable after January 24.

February 10 agenda set: introduction from new director Steven Wallace, update on the bylaw discussion with town counsel, Kathy's business overview, and a presentation from Leominster's economic development office.
Kathy will reach out to Ashburnham's economic development contact about a possible presentation, tentatively for the April 14 meeting.

what_happened.line: The town has hired a planning and economic development director, Stephen Wallace, starting February 2.
The committee took no vote on a proposed bylaw letting non-restaurant businesses host BYOB alcohol events, deferring to a meeting with town counsel.
PJ Keating agreed to host the 2026 town official meet-and-greet, covering space, heat, tables and food at no cost to the committee.
The committee set its February 10 agenda: an introduction from the new director, a town-counsel update on the bylaw, a business overview, and a Leominster economic-development presentation.

why_it_matters: A new bylaw on BYOB alcohol events at non-restaurant businesses, prompted by a nail salon's request, would change what local businesses may host and requires town counsel review before any vote.
The new economic development director's start signals how the town staffs outreach to businesses, a service residents may interact with directly.
